request.system:
You are a senior code reviewer. You review one group of related change units from a pull request and report the problems a careful reviewer would raise: bugs, broken contracts, missing error handling, security holes, data loss, races, and risky code without tests.

Rules:
- Report findings only. Never restate, summarise or praise the diff.
- Anchor every finding to a file path and a line number printed in the diff: the new-side number, or the old-side number for a deleted line.
- One finding per problem. "claim" is one sentence; "fix" is a short suggested change.
- severity: "high" breaks callers, loses data or opens a security hole; "medium" is a likely bug or missing handling; "low" is a minor risk.
- Never invent numbers, metrics, line numbers or code that is not shown.
- The hints are machine labels (probabilities 0-1, risk 1-5). Use them to decide where to look, not as facts.
- The Context section, when present, is unchanged background (callers, types, tests, config). Report a finding there only when the change breaks it, anchored to the changed line that causes it.
- verdict: "approve" when nothing needs changing, "comment" for low findings or questions only, "request_changes" when a finding must be fixed before merging.
- confidence: a number from 0 to 1, how sure you are that the findings and the verdict are right given what you were shown.

Answer with JSON only, no prose and no code fence, in exactly this shape:
{"findings":[{"file":"path/to/file","line":12,"severity":"low|medium|high","claim":"one sentence","fix":"suggested fix"}],"verdict":"approve|comment|request_changes","confidence":0.8}
Use "findings": [] when there is nothing to report.

Security focus: check authentication and authorisation paths, secrets or personal data reaching logs, responses or storage, injection, unsafe deserialisation, and money handling (rounding, double charges).

Performance focus: look for I/O or queries inside loops, unbounded work, missing batching or pagination, blocking calls on hot or async paths, and races between concurrent callers.

result.text: {"findings":[{"file":"web/src/components/ProfilePage.tsx","line":4,"severity":"medium","claim":"ProfilePage switches from `useUser`, which exposed `error`, to `useProfileCache`, whose effect does `.catch(() => {})` and leaves `loading` true, so a failed profile load now shows an endless spinner instead of an error.","fix":"Have `useProfileCache` store and return the load error and clear `loading` on failure, then render that error in ProfilePage."},{"file":"web/src/hooks/useUser.ts","line":22,"severity":"low","claim":"`error` is never cleared when `id` or `include` changes or a later fetch succeeds, so a stale error from a previous user persists alongside the new user.","fix":"Call `setError(null)` (and optionally `setUser(null)`) at the start of the effect, or clear the error on success."},{"file":"web/src/hooks/useUser.ts","line":20,"severity":"low","claim":"`.then(setUser)` is not guarded by the abort signal, so if `getUser` resolves after `ctrl.abort()` the previous user can overwrite state after an id change.","fix":"Use `.then((u) => { if (!ctrl.signal.aborted) setUser(u); })`."},{"file":"web/src/components/ProfileHeader.tsx","line":26,"severity":"low","claim":"The refresh button has no `type` attribute, so if ProfileHeader is rendered inside the profile edit form, clicking it submits the form.","fix":"Add `type=\"button\"`."}],"verdict":"request_changes","confidence":0.6}

findings.claim: The refresh button has no `type` attribute, so if ProfileHeader is rendered inside the profile edit form, clicking it submits the form.

ProfilePage switches from `useUser`, which exposed `error`, to `useProfileCache`, whose effect does `.catch(() => {})` and leaves `loading` true, so a failed profile load now shows an endless spinner instead of an error.
findings.fix: Have `useProfileCache` store and return the load error and clear `loading` on failure, then render that error in ProfilePage.

findings.claim: `.then(setUser)` is not guarded by the abort signal, so if `getUser` resolves after `ctrl.abort()` the previous user can overwrite state after an id change.
`error` is never cleared when `id` or `include` changes or a later fetch succeeds, so a stale error from a previous user persists alongside the new user.
findings.fix: Call `setError(null)` (and optionally `setUser(null)`) at the start of the effect, or clear the error on success.
